cards.explanation: The answer is False. Paul says, "We always thank God for all of you, remembering you in our prayers" Always! Not once in a while, not when it's convenient. That's a team that keeps the thank-you going, friends.

The answer is our Lord Jesus Christ. Paul says it's their "…enduring hope in our Lord Jesus Christ." Notice that word enduring, friends. It means this hope lasts, like an oven that holds its heat through the whole bake. And it has the right Person holding it up.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "Brothers who are beloved by God, we know that He has chosen you…" Beloved by God, and chosen. Sit with that for a second, friends, because it's a lot of good news in one sentence.

The answer is power and the Holy Spirit. Paul says the gospel came "…not only in word, but also in power, in the Holy Spirit, and with great conviction…" It wasn't just talk, friends. Power, the Holy Spirit and great conviction all came along with the word.

The answer is suffering. Paul says they welcomed the message "…with the joy of the Holy Spirit, in spite of your great suffering." Joy and great suffering in the same sentence, friends. That tells you this joy wasn't coming from easy days.

The answer is Paul's team and the Lord. Paul writes, "…you became imitators of us and of the Lord…" They watched how Paul's team lived and they followed. Same way my cookie cutter kids learned to press clean and lift straight, friends, by watching somebody do it first.

The answer is example. Paul says, "…you have become an example to all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia." They went from learning to being the ones people learn from. That's a good day for any student, friends.
The answer is False. Paul says "…your faith in God has gone out to every place…" (1 Thessalonians 1:8). It didn't stay inside Macedonia and Achaia, friends. It went well past them.

The answer is that Paul's team has no need to say anything more. Paul says their faith "…has gone out to every place, so that we have no need to say anything more." Their lives were already doing the talking, friends. I'd love a cookie that advertised itself that well.

The answer is idols. Paul says they "…turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God" Idols on one side, the living and true God on the other. That's a real turn, friends, not a little nudge.
The answer is God's Son. Paul says they "…await His Son from heaven…" The Son is the One they're waiting on, friends. And that's the very reason my ovens stay ready.

The answer is True. Paul says they await His Son from heaven, "…whom He raised from the dead…" God raised Him from the dead, and that's the Son they're waiting for. What a thing to look forward to, friends.
